content.title: Justin Rose
content.text: Bio Rose broke through to win the 2013 U.S. Open at Merion Golf Club for his first major title. In the summer of 2016, he made history again by becoming golf's first Olympic gold medalist in 112 years as he edged Henrik Stenson by two strokes in Rio de Janeiro. He ended a four-year victory drought on the PGA Tour in 2024 when he claimed the AT&T National Pro-Am at Pebble Beach. Rose was 17 when he made his major championship debut in 1998 at The Open Championship at Royal Birkdale, tying for fourth place thanks to a dramatic pitch-in on the 72nd hole. He owns 27 worldwide wins, 13 of which have come on the PGA Tour. On the first day of February 2026, Rose posted an impressive seven-stroke victory in the Farmers Insurance Open at Torrey Pines, posting a record total of 23-under-par 265. In April 2025, he lost a playoff to Rory McIlroy at the Masters Tournament, despite shooting a final-round 66 that included 10 birdies. He also lost a sudden-death playoff to Sergio Garcia in the 2017 Masters, and he was the runner-up in the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon. When Rose won the 2019 Farmers Insurance Open at Torrey Pines, site of two U.S. Opens, he was the No. 1 player in the Official World Golf Ranking. He represented Great Britain and Ireland in the 1997 Walker Cup. He also has been a member of seven European Ryder Cup teams.
